name: Government ethics
definition: Rules and norms about how people who hold public power may use it, and who checks them.
scope: Conflicts of interest, disclosure, clemency, appointments and the limits on each. Electoral rules and campaign finance have their own topics.

name: Public office and private gain
definition: Whether, and how, the law should stop officeholders and their families from using an office to make money.
scope: Holdings and trading rules, family appointments, published tax returns and the reversal of pardons. Bribery statutes and lobbying rules belong to neighbouring topics.
axis: favors stricter rules against officials profiting from their office; negative favors leaving officials free to own and trade as any other citizen does

name: Business & Economy
definition: Beliefs about how people trade, work, invest and are paid, and what the law should do about it.

name: Business
definition: Business covers how companies are owned, governed and run, and whom they must answer to.

name: Finance
definition: Finance covers banking, lending, investing and the markets where money changes hands.

name: Trade
definition: Trade covers the buying and selling of goods and services across national borders and the barriers governments place on it.
axis: favors open trade with few barriers, negative favors tariffs and protection for home industries.

name: Jobs
definition: Jobs covers pay, hiring, firing and working conditions, and how much of that the law should set.

name: Consumer Protection
definition: Consumer Protection covers the rules that govern what companies may sell to the public and how they must treat the people who buy from them.
axis: favors stronger government rules protecting buyers, negative favors fewer rules and leaving buyers and sellers to sort things out.

name: Computers & Internet
definition: Beliefs about software, networks and the rules that govern them.

name: Internet
definition: How the internet is run and who sets its rules, from the companies that carry traffic to the laws that govern access, speech and content.

name: Software
definition: How programs are built, licensed, sold and maintained, and how much control the people who use them get over what runs on their devices.

name: Privacy and Data
definition: How personal information is collected, stored, shared and protected by companies and governments, and what people can do about it.

name: Games
definition: Video games, how they are made and sold, how they make money, and what effect they have on the people who play them.

name: Artificial Intelligence
definition: Computer systems that learn from data to write, draw, predict and decide, and the rules for how they are built and used.
axis: favors stronger limits and oversight on how AI is built and used; negative favors letting it develop and spread with fewer restrictions.

name: News & Media
definition: Beliefs about how news is made, paid for and trusted.

name: Newspapers
definition: How printed and online newspapers gather news, pay for it, and reach readers, and whether they still matter as institutions.

name: Television
definition: Broadcast and cable television news, including who owns it, how it is regulated, and whether it leaves viewers better informed.

name: Radio
definition: AM, FM, satellite, and public radio as sources of news, including talk radio and local stations.

name: Social Media
definition: How social platforms spread news, decide who sees what, and what they owe the public and the publishers whose work they carry.
axis: favors platforms taking, or being made to take, more responsibility for the news they spread (paying publishers, labeling, moderating); negative favors platforms as open pipes with as little interference as possible.

name: Press Freedom
definition: The legal and practical protections journalists have from governments, courts, and powerful private parties, and the limits on what they may publish and how they get it.
axis: favors stronger and broader protections for journalists and publishers; negative favors more limits on, or more accountability for, what journalists publish and how they obtain it.

name: Entertainment
definition: Beliefs about film, music, humor and the industries behind them.

name: Movies
definition: Feature films and the business that makes, releases and shows them, from theaters to streaming services.

name: Music
definition: Recorded and live music, the people who make it, and the labels, streaming services and platforms that carry it to listeners.

name: Humor
definition: Comedy in stand-up, film, television and online, and the arguments over what jokes are acceptable and who decides.

name: Publishing
definition: The business of producing and selling books, from traditional publishing houses to self-publishing and ebooks.

name: Recreation & Sports
definition: Beliefs about sport, travel, cars and the outdoors.

name: Sports
definition: Sports covers how organized athletics, from youth leagues to professional teams, are run, funded and regulated, and what they do to the people who play and watch them.

name: Travel
definition: Travel covers how people move around for leisure and what tourism does to travelers, to the places they visit and to the wider world.

name: Autos
definition: Autos covers cars and driving: how vehicles are built, powered and regulated, and how much of daily life should depend on them.

name: Outdoors
definition: Outdoors covers hunting, fishing, hiking, camping and other recreation on natural land, and how that land is managed and shared.

name: Health
definition: Beliefs about disease, treatment, fitness and the systems that deliver care.

name: Diseases
definition: How societies prevent, detect, and respond to illness, from infectious outbreaks to chronic conditions like cancer and diabetes.

name: Drugs
definition: Prescription medicines, over-the-counter products, and recreational substances, including how they are approved, priced, sold, and regulated.

name: Fitness
definition: Exercise, physical activity, and the habits and products people use to stay in shape and stay able-bodied as they age.

name: Medicine
definition: How doctors and other clinicians diagnose and treat patients, and how medical knowledge is judged, standardized, and applied.

name: Health Insurance
definition: How the cost of medical care is pooled and paid, whether through private plans, employers, individual payment, or government programs.

name: Government
definition: Beliefs about how public power is won, held, used and checked.

name: Elections
definition: How voters choose officeholders, including who may vote, how ballots are cast and counted, and how campaigns are run.

name: Military
definition: How a country raises, funds, and uses its armed forces, and who decides when they fight.
axis: favors a larger military that is used more readily; negative favors a smaller force used with more restraint.

name: Law
definition: How laws are enforced and judged, including policing, courts, bail, and punishment.

name: Taxes
definition: How government raises money from people and businesses, including who pays, how much, and on what.
axis: favors higher or broader taxation; negative favors lower or narrower taxation.

name: Regional
definition: Beliefs that belong to one place: a country, a region, a state or a city.

name: Countries
definition: Beliefs about the direction, policies, or condition of a single nation taken as a whole.

name: Regions
definition: Beliefs about a part of a country, or an area that crosses borders, that is larger than one city but not a whole sovereign country.

name: U.S. States
definition: Beliefs about policies and choices made at the level of an individual American state.

name: Cities
definition: Beliefs about how a particular city should be built, run, or paid for.

name: Society & Culture
definition: Beliefs about people, communities, the environment and belief itself.

name: People
definition: People covers human nature, personal character, and how much of a person's life is shaped by their own choices as opposed to the circumstances they were born into.

name: Environment
definition: Environment covers how people should use, protect, and share natural resources such as land, air, water, wildlife, and the climate.

name: Religion
definition: Religion covers the role of faith, religious institutions, and religious belief in personal life, community life, and public decisions.
axis: holds that religion is good for people and society and deserves a larger public role, negative holds that religion does harm or should stay a private matter.

name: Family
definition: Family covers marriage, parenting, household structure, and the duties people owe to their relatives.

name: Crime and Justice
definition: Crime and Justice covers how society should prevent crime, punish people who commit it, and treat both victims and the accused.

name: Education
definition: Beliefs about schools, universities and how people learn.

name: College and University
definition: Covers education after high school at colleges and universities: who should attend, what it should teach, how it is run, and whether it is worth what it costs.

name: K-12
definition: Covers schooling from kindergarten through high school: what is taught, how schools are run and funded, and how families choose among them.

name: Teaching
definition: Covers how teachers are trained, paid, evaluated and supported, and how much control they have over what happens in their classrooms.

name: Student Debt
definition: Covers loans taken out to pay for college, how they are repaid, and who should bear the cost when borrowers cannot.

name: Arts & Humanities
definition: Beliefs about art, history, literature and philosophy.

name: Photography
definition: Photography covers how pictures are made with a camera, how they are edited and shown, and how they should be judged as art or as records.

name: History
definition: History covers how the past is studied, written, taught and remembered in public, including monuments, textbooks and popular retellings.

name: Literature
definition: Literature covers what people read, how books are judged and taught, and what fiction and poetry are for.

name: Philosophy
definition: Philosophy covers the big questions about knowledge, right and wrong, meaning and the mind, and the question of whether thinking about them carefully is worth doing.

name: Science
definition: Beliefs about what is known about the natural world and how.

name: Animals
definition: Animals covers what is known about how other animals think, feel and behave, and how much their inner lives resemble ours.

name: Astronomy
definition: Astronomy covers what is known about planets, stars, galaxies and the universe beyond Earth, including whether life exists elsewhere.

name: Engineering
definition: Engineering covers what is known about designing and building machines, structures and systems that work reliably in the real world.

name: Climate
definition: Climate covers what is known about how Earth's climate works, how much it is changing, why, and what can be predicted about it.

name: Physics
definition: Physics covers what is known about matter, energy, space and time, and how far its current theories and big experiments can be trusted.

name: Social Science
definition: Beliefs about how people behave, alone and together.

name: Languages
definition: How people learn, use, and pass on languages, and how societies decide which languages get taught, protected, or left to fade.

name: Archaeology
definition: The study of past human life through physical remains, and the rules about who may dig up, keep, and display what is found.

name: Psychology
definition: How the mind works, why people feel and act as they do, and how mental health problems are understood and treated.

name: Economics
definition: How people produce, trade, and share goods and money, and what government should do about markets, prices, and wages.

name: Sociology
definition: How groups, institutions, and social forces shape the way people live, and what holds communities together or pulls them apart.

name: Reference
definition: Definitions, statistics and quotations the other topics rest on.

name: Dictionaries
definition: How dictionaries decide which words and meanings to include, and whether their job is to describe how people use words or to set a standard for correct use.

name: Statistics
definition: How statistics are produced, reported and used in public argument, and how much trust they deserve compared with other ways of knowing.

name: Quotations
definition: How quotations are attributed, checked and used as authority in argument and in reference works.

name: Core Principles
definition: The principles the other positions on this site are argued from.

name: Democracy & Rule of Law
definition: How elections, courts and the constitution keep power answerable, and how to strengthen them.

name: Rights & Liberty
definition: The freedoms the law protects and the responsibilities that come with them.

name: Evidence & Process
definition: How public decisions should be made: on evidence, with scorecards, and with a view to the wider world.

name: Energy
definition: How energy is produced, priced and researched.

name: Immigration
definition: Who may come to the country, on what terms, and how the rules are enforced.
axis: favors more immigration; negative favors less, down to halting it

name: Caitlin Clark
definition: Beliefs about Caitlin Clark: her effect on the WNBA's audience and money, how she is treated on the court and in coverage, and where she stands among players.
axis: Clark's arrival explains the WNBA's growth and she is treated unfairly for it; negative means the growth has broader causes and the treatment is ordinary

name: Greatest of all time
definition: Beliefs ranking athletes against each other across eras: who was the best, and what best means.

name: Sports and money
definition: Beliefs about what money does to sports: pay, betting, college athletes and the fans who pay for it all.
axis: money has made the sport better; negative means it has made it worse

name: Movies and television
definition: Beliefs about what is on screen: franchises, remakes, streaming, awards and what is worth watching.

name: Popular music
definition: Beliefs about the music most people listen to: who is great, what streaming did, and whether the old days were better.

name: Everyday arguments
definition: The arguments people have for fun and keep having: food, manners and the small rules of daily life.

name: Online life
definition: Beliefs about what living online does to people: phones, feeds, children, attention and truth.
axis: social media and phones do more good than harm; negative means more harm

name: Art and machines
definition: Beliefs about machine-made art, writing and music: whether it is art, whether it should be sold, and what it does to the people who used to make those things.
axis: machine-made work is legitimate art and good for culture; negative means it is not
